questions.question: Which of the following forts was built by the Kakatiya dynasty?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Golconda.__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Golkonda Fort was built by the Kakatiya dynasty in the 13th century.**
 
• It is also known as **Shepherd's Hill" or "Golla Konda".**
 
• Muhammad Quli Qutab Shah established Hyderabad in 1591 to extend the capital beyond the fortified Golconda.
 
• Initially, the Kakatiyas ruled over a small territory near Warangal. Over time, they **expanded their rule** to include most of the eastern Deccan region. 
 
 
• They ruled over a significant region in South India, with **Warangal as their capital.**
 
• It encompassed present-day Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, parts of eastern Karnataka, and southern Odisha.
 
 
 
• **Rudradeva I** founded a sovereign kingdom in** 1163 CE.**
 
• The most powerful rulers of the dynasty were** Ganapathi Deva and Rudramadevi.**
 
• The dynasty worshipped the **goddess Kakati.**
 
• The family was called** Kakatiyas.**
 
• The Kakatiyas also worshipped** Svayambhuva, i.e., Siva.​**

questions.question: Which of the following dynasties established the Vijayanagara kingdom in fourteenth century?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Sangama dynasty**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sangama dynasty** was the founding dynasty of the **Vijayanagara Empire**, established in the **14th century**.
 
• The empire was founded in **1336 CE** by two brothers, **Harihara I** and **Bukka Raya I**, who were previously commanders under the Hoysala Empire.
 
• The Vijayanagara Empire played a crucial role in the preservation of **Hindu culture and traditions** during a time of Islamic invasions in South India.
 
• The Sangama dynasty ruled until the mid-15th century, when it was succeeded by the **Saluva dynasty**.
 
• The empire's capital, **Vijayanagara**, was located near the modern-day city of **Hampi in Karnataka**, which is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
• The Vijayanagara Empire contributed significantly to **art, architecture, and literature**, including the construction of iconic monuments like the **Virupaksha Temple**.
 
• The Sangama dynasty's rule marked the beginning of the empire's development as a major power in South India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Aravidu dynasty**__

 __
 
• The **Aravidu dynasty** was the fourth and final dynasty to rule the Vijayanagara Empire.
 
• It was established in the late **16th century** by **Aliya Rama Raya**, following the decline of the Tuluva dynasty.
 
• This dynasty saw the empire's eventual decline after the **Battle of Talikota** (1565), which led to the fall of Vijayanagara.
 
 
 
• **Saluva dynasty**__
 __
 
• The **Saluva dynasty** succeeded the Sangama dynasty in the late **15th century**.
 
• It was founded by **Saluva Narasimha Deva Raya**, who rose to power during a period of political instability.
 
• This dynasty laid the groundwork for the eventual rise of the Tuluva dynasty.
 
 
 
• **Tuluva dynasty**__
 
 
• The **Tuluva dynasty** was the third dynasty of the Vijayanagara Empire and is often considered its **golden age**.
 
• It was founded by **Veeranarasimha Raya** and reached its zenith under **Krishnadevaraya**, one of the most celebrated rulers of the empire.
 
• Krishnadevaraya expanded the empire and promoted advancements in **art, architecture, and literature**.

questions.question: In which of the following empires of South India was the Kamalapuram tank built in the 15th century?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Vijayanagara Empire**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Kamalapuram tank** is a well-known water reservoir constructed during the reign of the **Vijayanagara Empire** in the 15th century.
 
• This tank was built to provide **irrigation facilities** and to meet the **water needs of the capital city**, Hampi, which was one of the richest and most powerful cities of its time.
 
• The Vijayanagara Empire was renowned for its **advanced water management systems**, including tanks, canals, and aqueducts, which were vital for agriculture and urban needs.
 
• The Kamalapuram tank is located near the **Virupaksha Temple** and other significant architectural marvels of Hampi, showcasing the empire's focus on both functionality and aesthetics.
 
• It is an example of the **sophisticated engineering** and planning that characterized the Vijayanagara Empire, reflecting their understanding of **hydrology and sustainable practices**.
 
• The tank played an important role in maintaining the city's **agricultural productivity** and providing water to its residents, making it a critical component of the empire's infrastructure.
 
• The Vijayanagara Empire (1336–1646 CE) was one of the most significant empires in South India, known for its **architectural achievements**, **cultural contributions**, and **military prowess**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bidar Empire**__

 __
 
• The Bidar Sultanate was part of the **Deccan Sultanates** and was established in the 15th century.
 
• Bidar is known for its **fort** and **Bidriware** (a form of metal handicraft).
 
• Though the Bidar Sultanate contributed to architecture and culture, it did not play a significant role in water management like the Vijayanagara Empire.
 
 
 
• **Bijapur Empire**__
 __
 
• The Bijapur Sultanate, another member of the **Deccan Sultanates**, is renowned for its **Islamic architecture**, including the iconic **Gol Gumbaz**.
 
• While Bijapur excelled in architecture, its contributions were more focused on **monuments** rather than large-scale water management systems like those in the Vijayanagara Empire.
 
 
 
• **Chola Empire**__
 
 
• The Chola Empire (9th–13th century CE) is famous for its **temple architecture**, such as the **Brihadeeswarar Temple** in Tamil Nadu.
 
• They were pioneers in **irrigation systems**, particularly in the Kaveri delta, but the Kamalapuram tank was not part of their contributions as it was built much later during the Vijayanagara period.

questions.question: Bahmani Monuments at Gulbarga, Karnataka represent ________ style of architecture.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Deccan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Bahmani monuments at Gulbarga, Karnataka, predominantly represent the Deccan style of architecture.
 
• The Deccan style was prominent during the period of the Bahmani Sultanate which existed from **1347 to 1527** in the Deccan region.
 
• This architectural style incorporates elements from Persian and local Deccan architecture, illustrating the diverse influences of that era.
 
• Gulbarga, the first capital of the Bahmani Sultanate, houses many important monuments such as the **Gulbarga fort and the Jama Masjid** within it, which are prime examples of the** Deccan architectural style**.
 
• The Deccan style can be seen in the simplicity of **design, use of arches, and distinct decorative elements.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mameluke**: This style pertains to the Mamluk Sultanate (Cairo), known for its architectural and cultural contributions, particularly in Egypt and the Levant. However, it is not directly connected to the Bahmani Sultanate.
 
• **Sikh**: Sikh architecture, known for its unique blend of Islamic and Hindu elements, primarily pertains to Sikh religious structures. It's not related to the Bahmani architectural style.
 
• **Nagara**: The Nagara style is a traditional Hindu architectural style that originated in northern India. It is characterized by beehive-shaped towers (shikharas) made up of layered horizontal sections, but is not associated with the Bahmani Sultanate's architectural style.

questions.question: Who among the following founded a suburban township near Vijayanagara, called Nagalapuram, after his mother?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Krishna Deva Raya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Krishna Deva Raya** was a prominent ruler of the Vijayanagara Empire who reigned from 1509 to 1529.
 
• He founded the suburban township of **Nagalapuram** in honor of his mother, Nagala Devi.
 
• Krishna Deva Raya was known for his administrative prowess, military strength, and contributions to art, culture, and architecture in South India.
 
• The Vijayanagara Empire flourished under his rule, becoming a major center for trade, culture, and religion.
 
• He also authored the Telugu literary work **Amuktamalyada**, showcasing his deep interest in literature and spirituality.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vijayanagara Empire:**

 
 
• The Vijayanagara Empire, established in 1336, was one of the most significant South Indian empires, known for its contributions to art, architecture, and economy.
 
• It served as a bulwark against Islamic invasions in South India and fostered a synthesis of Hindu culture and traditions.
 
• Hampi, the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire, is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
 
 
• **Krishna Deva Raya's Achievements:**
 
 
• He expanded the empire's territory through military campaigns, including victories over the Bahmani Sultanate and the Gajapati rulers of Odisha.
 
• His reign marked a golden age of prosperity, with advancements in trade, agriculture, and irrigation systems.
 
• He patronized several temples, including the famous Virupaksha Temple in Hampi.
 
 
 
• **Amuktamalyada:**
 
 
• Written in Telugu, Amuktamalyada is a poetic work by Krishna Deva Raya that narrates the story of the Tamil saint Andal.
 
• The text reflects his deep devotion to Lord Vishnu and his intellectual engagement with literature and spiritual philosophy.
 
 
 
• **Nagalapuram:**
 
 
• Nagalapuram, named after Nagala Devi (Krishna Deva Raya's mother), is located in present-day Andhra Pradesh.
 
• The town showcases the architectural and cultural advancements of the Vijayanagara Empire.

questions.question: The village servants or functionaries, who constituted of groups of families in Vijayanagar empire, were called ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**ayagars**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The term **ayagars** was used to refer to village servants or functionaries in the Vijayanagar Empire who performed essential administrative, economic, and social duties.
 
• Ayagars consisted of **12 hereditary roles**, including village accountants, priests, blacksmiths, barbers, and other service providers, ensuring the functioning of village administration.
 
• They were often paid through a share of the village produce or land grants known as **inam lands**.
 
• The ayagar system contributed to the decentralized governance model of the Vijayanagar Empire, ensuring efficient management at the village level.
 
• This system was crucial for maintaining agricultural productivity and social harmony in villages during the Vijayanagar period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vijayanagar Empire:**

 
 
• The Vijayanagar Empire was established in 1336 by Harihara and Bukka Raya and lasted until 1646.
 
• It was known for its contributions to art, architecture, literature, and efficient administration.
 
• The empire's capital was Hampi, now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
 
 
• **Decentralized Administration:**
 
 
• The Vijayanagar Empire employed a decentralized administrative structure, where local governance was carried out through village communities and ayagars.
 
• This system helped in effective management and ensured the welfare of the rural population.
 
 
 
• **Inam Lands:**
 
 
• Inam lands were tax-free lands granted to ayagars in exchange for their services to the community.
 
• These grants were hereditary and formed the basis of the ayagar system's sustainability.
 
 
 
• **Social Hierarchy:**
 
 
• The ayagars were integral to the hierarchical social structure, maintaining order and supporting agricultural and economic activities.
 
• They ensured the smooth functioning of villages and were accountable to the local rulers or administrators.

questions.question: The Bidar Fort of Karnataka is irregularly ______ in shape.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**rhomboid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Bidar Fort is located in Bidar, Karnataka, India and is known for its unique architecture.
 
• The fort is irregularly rhomboid in shape, featuring various bastions and structures within its perimeter.
 
• The fort was built in the 15th century by Sultan Ahmad Shah Wali Bahmani of the Bahmani Sultanate.
 
• Bidar Fort is a significant historical monument and has a combination of Persian and indigenous architectural styles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bidar**

 
 
• Bidar is a city in the northeastern part of Karnataka, India, known for its rich history and cultural heritage.
 
• The city is famous for its Bidriware, a form of metal handicraft that originated in the region.
 
• Bidar was once the capital of the Bahmani Sultanate and later the Barid Shahi dynasty.
 
 
 
• **Bahmani Sultanate**
 
 
• The Bahmani Sultanate was a Muslim state of the Deccan in South India and one of the major medieval Indian kingdoms.
 
• It was established in 1347 by Ala-ud-Din Bahman Shah.
 
• The sultanate is known for its contributions to art, architecture, and culture in the Deccan region.
 
 
 
• **Architectural Features of Bidar Fort**
 
 
• The fort includes various structures such as mosques, palaces, and large gateways.
 
• Notable features include the Rangin Mahal, Gagan Mahal, and the Takht Mahal.
 
• The fort’s design incorporates Persian architectural elements, evident in its intricate tile work and domes.
